question: Does reducing the explicit timestep reduce late frozen-problem oscillation?
interpretation: Fresh frozen-problem trajectories from the same field, not exact checkpoint restarts
comparison: Compare common artificial time through 6.36 and report work separately; terminal accepted state s has time s*dt
falsification: If oscillation persists at smaller dt, reject timestep reduction as a sufficient remedy in this tested range
limitations: Smaller updates alone are not convergence
A 6.36 artificial-time trajectory may still drift slowly
Normalized elastic gradient plus unscaled regularization is not assumed to be descent for the logged total objective
No claim of fixed-domain resolution refinement while the existing ladder keeps dx=1
